Description:
Boolean operations between two solids that occupy the SAME space. The answers are forced and need no
geometry: the difference is empty, and intersection and union are the body itself.

It takes three calls to build the interesting pair - make a sphere twice - and the sphere is what makes
it interesting. solid.sphere builds it from TWO faces, each bounded by four half circles like the seam
of a tennis ball, neither containing a pole, and the parameter axes of the two faces are perpendicular
to each other. Two identical spheres therefore have pairwise COINCIDENT faces, which is a special case
in its own right.

So the case asks the question twice:
  bigA / bigB   two identical spheres - the faces coincide pairwise
  rotA / rotB   the same, but the second sphere is turned by 37 degrees about the axis (1,2,3). Neither
                a standard axis nor a multiple of 90 degrees, so nothing about the sphere changes to
                look at, while its faces no longer line up with those of the first at all
The second pair is the harder one and the results show it: intersection and union come back with 4 faces
and 12 edges instead of 2 faces, because the two tennis ball seams cut each other.

Three sizes and two controls sit alongside, all of them differences that must be empty:
  r2Diff, r3Diff, r40Diff   the defect this case was written for used to alternate with the radius
  boxDiff                   two coincident boxes - coincidence by itself is not the trigger
  torDiff                   two coincident tori - a periodic surface by itself is not either
Expected:
bigDiff, rotDiff, r2Diff, r3Diff, r40Diff, boxDiff, torDiff   EMPTY, recorded as "exists": "false",
      which is what an empty boolean result looks like: nothing is stored under the name.
  bigInter, bigUnion, rotInter, rotUnion   the sphere itself, 4/3*pi*7^3 = 1436.7550402

The other radii, for the record: 4/3*pi*2^3 = 33.5103216, 4/3*pi*3^3 = 113.0973355 and
4/3*pi*40^3 = 268082.5731063.

The FACE COUNTS are the interesting part of the fingerprint here, more than the volumes:
  bigInter, bigUnion   2 faces - the operands' faces coincide pairwise, so nothing has to be cut
  rotInter, rotUnion   4 faces, 12 edges - the two tennis ball seams cross, and the result carries both
If rotInter ever comes back with 2 faces, the rotation has stopped taking effect and the second half of
the case is testing nothing.
Status:
OK since 2026-08-27. All three operations are right on both pairs.

The case was split off from HemisphereOnCylinderThreeWays, whose Status had carried the defect as a
recipe ("run this case, then ...") rather than as a case, which meant running that file never showed
it. Reducing it was worth the trouble: what it is about turned out not to be what it looked like there.
It is not about two solids that are the same point set but BUILT differently - a box measured against
the union of its own two halves works fine - it is about the sphere.

THE HISTORY, because each step corrected the picture of the one before.

As found: difference threw "The given key 'CADability.GeoObject.Face' was not present in the
dictionary", intersect failed on a Debug.Fail assertion, union worked. The difference only threw from
about radius 2.25 upward - 1.25 and 2.0 returned the correct empty result - and the position played no
part, radius 7 at (3,4,5) throwing just as at the origin. That size threshold suggested an absolute
tolerance somewhere; it was a red herring.

First repair: intersect fixed, difference then threw at EVERY radius including the two that had worked.

Second repair: no more exceptions anywhere, but the difference returned a solid of 4 spherical faces
enclosing about 1e-6 of volume at radius 2, 2.25, 3 and 40, while 1.25, 2.5, 5 and 7 came out empty.
The alternation looked like a mesh artefact and was not: the result was in principle correct - a sphere
with a hole that is exactly the sphere itself - because the difference branch never ran the emptiness
test at all. The whole BRep boolean works on faces, edges and vertices; the triangulation only enters
through that one volume test. Which is also why the alternation had nothing to do with triangulation.

Third repair, 2026-08-27: the test is there, and the difference comes back empty at every radius tried
(1.25, 2, 2.25, 2.5, 3, 5, 7, 40), with the intersection giving the full sphere in each case.

RE-RECORDED 2026-08-28 after the second BRep fix of that day (Shell.cs, Surface.cs and the new
SurfaceContacts.cs). The case failed against its old baseline both inside the suite and on its own,
so the change is systematic and not the batch contamination. It is a PARTITION change: faces on
periodic surfaces that used to be one face are now split into two.
What moved, for rotInter and rotUnion alike:
  faces       4  -> 6      surfaces  SphericalSurface:4 -> :6
  edges      12  -> 16     vertices  10 -> 12
  edgeLength 93.7444510817 -> 124.400722268
What did NOT move: the volume is the same to 1.5e-7 (1436.75084457 -> 1436.75105845) and the area to
2.4e-6, both far inside the tolerance, and extent, euler, closed and consistent are unchanged. So the
bodies are the same bodies, cut into more faces.
